from.place: Component-extension part of the supported localization triangle theorem.

title: Component maps extend to a triangle morphism (second variable)
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field, A a finite commutative ring, X,Y separated finite type k-schemes, K∈D⁺(X_et,A), L∈D⁺(Y_et,A), and assume F=K external tensor L is bounded below. For closed immersions B⊆X and C,D⊆Y, the three specified supported exterior products [def-pur-supported-exterior-product], on intersection support, original support and open support respectively, form a morphism from the normalized support triangle [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] in the second variable tensored on the left with RΓ_B(X,K) to the product support triangle. The intersection and open components are transported by the canonical comparisons [def-pur-supported-localization-comparisons]. All three components are exactly those in the unchanged attached Lean statement.

source.place: Tag 09XP and Tag 0F1E; compatibility of the supported pairing with localization boundaries.

proof.text: Apply naturality under normalized inclusions of supports. Compose the product-intersection equality comparison with the target inclusion; the kernel-inclusion normalization identifies this composite with the product of the source inclusion and the identity in the fixed variable. Derived functoriality proves the first triangle square.

Compose the target restriction with its prescribed third isomorphism. Functoriality of support transport under successive open pullbacks identifies it with restriction to the actual product open. The already proved open naturality square, after canceling that isomorphism, is the second triangle square.
Use the corresponding connecting-map equation. Assemble the three prescribed components and three verified commutation equations into TriangleMorphism; the component equalities are reflexive.
